notes: Identity checked independently: title “If you like it, does it matter if it’s real?”, Felipe De Brigard, Philosophical Psychology 23(1), February 2010, pp. 43–57, DOI 10.1080/09515080903532290 match the neutral original reference. Supplied text contains the primary article, methods/results, notes, and references, rather than an abstract or secondary report. The p. 48 first-study result points to note 3, which supplies the only inferential test for the three-condition comparison. This is the omnibus test, not an invented pairwise odds ratio. The source reports percentages by condition but no OR in the inspected first-study results or inferential note; retain the printed test statistic instead of converting it. The canonical text encodes the statistic symbol as U+001F followed by 2, and equals signs as ¼; metric and test_statistic preserve that exact encoding. The numeric statistic, N, and p are explicit. No source PDF was supplied, so the damaged glyph could not be visually checked. The methods on pp. 46–47 state three conditions with 24 participants in each and each participant receiving only one vignette; no N sum is needed because note 3 explicitly prints N=72. The later Second Neutral follow-up (80 participants, p. 49) is a separate study and is excluded. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders.
